tb-E403-3.question:
Which of the following statements about X-ray radiographic imaging is/are correct?

(1) It produces images by measuring the intensity of X-rays passing through a patient’s body.

(2) Barium is used as an artificial contrast medium because it emits ionizing radiation.

(3) The body structures that reflect most X-rays appear white in an X-ray image.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E403-3.reasoning:
An artificial contrast medium should have a high linear attenuation coefficient and should not emit ionizing radiation.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

The body structures that attenuate most X-rays appear white in an X-ray image.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-E403-4.question:
Figure b shows the change in intensity I when an X-ray beam travels in two gases P and Q.

P and Q are gases of the same element but with different densities. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The half-value thickness of P is smaller than that of Q.

(2) The linear attenuation coefficient of P is smaller than that of Q.

(3) The density of P is lower than that of Q.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-E403-4.reasoning:
The intensity of an X-ray beam drops more slowly when travelling in gas P. Therefore, P has a larger half-value thickness and a smaller linear attenuation coefficient.

∴ (1) is incorrect. (2) is correct.

As P has a smaller linear attenuation coefficient, it has a lower density.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-E403-8.question:
The biological half-life of a radionuclide is much longer than its physical half-life. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The effective half-life of the radionuclide is approximately equal to the physical half-life.

(2) Before most of the radionuclides has decayed, only a small proportion has been removed from the body.

(3) This radioisotope is suitable for medical imaging even if it decays to an unstable nuclide.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E403-8.reasoning:
Consider 1te = 1tp + 1tb.

When tb is much larger than tp, 1tb is much smaller than 1tp. Therefore, 1te ≈ 1tp, i.e. te ≈ tp.

∴ (1) is correct.

As the biological half-life is much longer than the physical half-life, the number of radionuclides that has been removed from the body by biological processes is much less than the number of radionuclides that has decayed in the same period of time.

∴ (2) is correct.

Problems for disposal may arise if the radioisotope decays to an unstable nuclide.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-E403-22.question:
Connie takes two medical images of her liver. Figure p shows the image from CT examination and Figure q shows the one from ultrasound scanning.

(a) (i) Explain how a tomograph is produced in CT scanning. (3 marks)

(ii) Explain how the image in Figure p is constructed from tomographs. (2 marks)

(b) State what the light areas indicate in each image. (2 marks)

(c) State one advantage of ultrasound scanning over CT scanning. (1 mark)
tb-E403-22.answer:
(a) (i) The X-ray tube and X-ray detector rotate round a slice of body to obtain multiple attenuation profiles. 1A

The profiles are used to produce a map of attenuation coefficients of different body tissues by back projection algorithm. 1A

The map is then filled different shades of grey to form a tomograph of the slice of body. A region is filled darker if the attenuation coefficient there is smaller. 1A

(ii) Tomographs at different levels along the body are stacked and an attenuation coefficient map of a 3-D block is obtained. 1A

The image in Figure p is produced by digitally cutting through the 3-D attenuation coefficient map and looking at the cross-section from a certain direction. 1A

(b) In the CT image, the light areas indicate the body parts with high linear attenuation coefficient. 1A

In the ultrasound image, the light areas indicate the interfaces with high intensity reflection coefficient. 1A

(c) Ultrasound scanning does not involve ionizing radiation. 1A
